(declare-const x Int)

(assert (= l (cons x (cons y nil))))
(assert (= (head (tail l)) 5))
(assert (= (+ x y) 8))
(assert (or (= r nil) (> (head r) (+ x y))))
(assert (not (= r nil)))
(check-sat)

(assert (not (= r nil)))

(assert (not (= r nil)))

name: dpllt_intro solve
body:
; The classic DPLL(T) introduction example (Reynolds, VTSA 2017):
;   (x+1 > 0 or x+y > 0) and (x < 0 or x+y > 4) and not (x+y > 0)
; Propositionally satisfiable, but LIA-unsatisfiable: the theory solver
; rejects the context {x+1>0, not x+y>0, x<0} and adds the theory lemma
; (not x+1>0 or not x<0); after backtracking, {x+1>0, not x+y>0, x+y>4}
; is rejected as well.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (or (> (+ x 1) 0) (> (+ x y) 0)))
(assert (or (< x 0) (> (+ x y) 4)))
(assert (not (> (+ x y) 0)))

; cons(x, nil) = cons(y, z) gives x = y and z = nil (constructors are
; injective), so x = green. Then x = red is false and x != y is false:
; the second assertion fails, UNSAT.
(declare-datatypes ((Color 0)) (((red) (green) (blue))))
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Color) (tail List)))))
(declare-const x Color)
(declare-const y Color)
(declare-const z List)
(assert (= y green))
(assert (or (= x red) (not (= x y))))
(assert (= (cons x nil) (cons y z)))
(check-sat)

; Step-by-step example: deciding x > y forces x + 1 < y (F2), which LIA
; rejects. Conflict analysis learns not(x > y); after backtracking it
; propagates x > y to false, then F1 and F3 force x > z and z > y, which LIA
; also rejects: unsatisfiable.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (> x z)))
(assert (or (< (+ x 1) y) (not (> x y))))
(assert (or (> x y) (> z y)))
(check-sat)

OPTIONS 
; Step-by-step example: deciding x > y forces x + 1 < y (F2), which LIA
; rejects. Conflict analysis learns not(x > y); after backtracking it
; propagates x > y to false, then F1 and F3 force x > z and z > y, which LIA
; also rejects: unsatisfiable.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (> x z)))
(assert (or (< (+ x 1) y) (not (> x y))))
(assert (or (> x y) (> z y)))
(check-sat)

(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (> x z)))
(assert (or (< (+ x 1) y) (not (> x y))))
(assert (or (> x y) (> z y)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; Step-by-step example: deciding x > y forces x + 1 < y (F2), which LIA
; rejects. Conflict analysis learns not(x > y); after backtracking it
; propagates x > y to false, then F1 and F3 force x > z and z > y, which LIA
; also rejects: unsatisfiable.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (> x z)))
(assert (or (< (+ x 1) y) (not (> x y))))
(assert (or (> x y) (> z y)))
(check-sat)

name: lia_branch solve
body:
; LIA: branch and bound. 2x + 3y = 1 has rational solutions in the box
; [0,3] x [0,3] (x = 1/2, y = 0), but no integer ones. gcd(2,3) = 1, so
; only branching (splits on x <= k) proves it.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= (+ (* 2 x) (* 3 y)) 1))
(assert (and (>= x 0) (<= x 3) (>= y 0) (<= y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; LIA: branch and bound. 2x + 3y = 1 has rational solutions in the box
; [0,3] x [0,3] (x = 1/2, y = 0), but no integer ones. gcd(2,3) = 1, so
; only branching (splits on x <= k) proves it.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= (+ (* 2 x) (* 3 y)) 1))
(assert (and (>= x 0) (<= x 3) (>= y 0) (<= y 3)))
(check-sat)

body:
DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS no-theory-propagation finish
; LIA: branch and bound. 2x + 3y = 1 has rational solutions in the box
; [0,3] x [0,3] (x = 1/2, y = 0), but no integer ones. gcd(2,3) = 1, so
; only branching (splits on x <= k) proves it.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= (+ (* 2 x) (* 3 y)) 1))
(assert (and (>= x 0) (<= x 3) (>= y 0) (<= y 3)))
(check-sat)

OPTIONS 
; LIA: branch and bound. 2x + 3y = 1 has rational solutions in the box
; [0,3] x [0,3] (x = 1/2, y = 0), but no integer ones. gcd(2,3) = 1, so
; only branching (splits on x <= k) proves it.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= (+ (* 2 x) (* 3 y)) 1))
(assert (and (>= x 0) (<= x 3) (>= y 0) (<= y 3)))
(check-sat)

(assert (<= x 3))

(check-sat)

(assert (<= x 3))
(assert (or (<= y 6) (< (+ x y) 0)))
(check-sat)

; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS no-theory-propagation finish
; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

body:
DECISIONS u1 u2 u3 5 7
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS u1 u2 u3 -5
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS u1 u2 u3 -5 -7
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS 
; Nelson-Oppen with decisions: two one-element lists and their sum.
;   l = [x],  m = [y],  x + y = 10,  head(m) >= 1,
;   (l = m  or  x > y),  (x > 6  or  y < 3)
; Suggested path in the Playground:
;   l = m := true   -> DT (injectivity) derives x = y and gives it to LIA
;   x > 6 := true   -> LIA: x = y and x + y = 10 force x = 5. Conflict.
;   Backtrack       -> learned clause forces x <= 6, then y < 3. Conflict again.
;   Backtrack       -> x > 6 and x != y now hold at level 0.
;   l = m := false  -> x > y; satisfiable: l = [9], m = [1].
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const l List)
(declare-const m List)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(assert (= l (cons x nil)))
(assert (= m (cons y nil)))
(assert (= (+ x y) 10))
(assert (>= (head m) 1))
(assert (or (= l m) (> x y)))
(assert (or (> x 6) (< y 3)))
(check-sat)

DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS no-theory-propagation finish
; Non-convex combination (Nelson–Oppen needs case splits on the arrangement).
; DT: three singleton lists must be pairwise different, so their heads must be.
; LIA: the heads only range over {1, 2}. Neither theory alone derives an
; equality between x, y, z, but every arrangement fails.
(declare-datatypes ((List 0)) (((nil) (cons (head Int) (tail List)))))
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (and (>= x 1) (<= x 2) (>= y 1) (<= y 2) (>= z 1) (<= z 2)))
(assert (distinct (cons x nil) (cons y nil) (cons z nil)))
(check-sat)

(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (and (>= x 1) (<= x 2) (>= y 1) (<= y 2) (>= z 1) (<= z 2)))
(assert (distinct (cons x nil) (cons y nil) (cons z nil)))
(check-sat)

name: several_decisions finish
body:
DECISIONS 
LEMMAS 
OPTIONS finish
; Several decisions, two theory conflicts, two learned clauses (Playground).
; A path to try:  x > y := true,  x + z >= 10 := false,  w > x := false
;   -> x <= 3 and z >= 4 are forced; LIA: x > y > z >= 4 needs x >= 6. Conflict.
; Backtrack (keeps the learned clause, which forces w > x), then z >= 4 := true
;   -> LIA: x > y > z >= 4 needs x + z >= 10. Conflict.
; Backtrack again: z < 4 is forced and every assertion is true: sat.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(declare-const w Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (>= z 4) (< w 0)))
(assert (or (not (> x y)) (> y z) (>= (+ x z) 10)))
(assert (or (not (> y z)) (<= x 3) (> w x)))
(assert (or (not (>= z 4)) (<= (+ y z) 2) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(assert (or (not (<= x 3)) (> w x) (>= z 4)))
(assert (or (> w x) (< w 0) (>= (+ x z) 10) (> y z)))
(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)

(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)

(declare-const z Int)

(assert (or (> w x) (< w 0) (>= (+ x z) 10) (> y z)))
(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)

; Backtrack (keeps the learned clause, which forces w > x), then z >= 4 := true
;   -> LIA: x > y > z >= 4 needs x + z >= 10. Conflict.
; Backtrack again: z < 4 is forced and every assertion is true: sat.
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(declare-const w Int)

(declare-const x Int)

(declare-const z Int)

(assert (or (not (> x y)) (> y z) (>= (+ x z) 10)))

(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)

(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)

(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(declare-const w Int)
(assert (or (> x y) (>= z 4) (< w 0)))
(assert (or (not (> x y)) (> y z) (>= (+ x z) 10)))

(assert (or (not (>= z 4)) (<= (+ y z) 2) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))

(assert (or (> w x) (< w 0) (>= (+ x z) 10) (> y z)))
(assert (or (not (>= (+ x z) 10)) (<= x 3) (< w 0)))
(check-sat)
